title: California Insurance Code Section 10127.8 (advertising of term life insurance directed to people aged 55 or older)
updateCadence: Amended only by legislation. The section credit on the official host at the time of access read Added by Stats. 1988, Ch. 1473, Sec. 1.
claims: Section 10127.8(a) states that the purpose of the section is to assure truthful and adequate disclosure of all material and relevant information in the advertising of term life insurance which the commissioner, on the basis of an assessment of the total advertisement, determines is directed to individuals 55 years of age or older.

Section 10127.8(b) requires advertisements for term life insurance directed to individuals 55 years of age or older to clearly and prominently distinguish basic life insurance benefits from supplemental benefits such as accidental death benefits, and to prominently disclose any limitations, exceptions, or reductions affecting each benefit.

Section 10127.8(b)(3) requires such advertisements to prominently disclose any condition affecting continued insurability, and provides that if term coverage terminates at a stated age, or at the end of any designated period, that fact and the specified age or designated period shall be disclosed.

Section 10127.8(b)(4) and (5) require such advertisements to prominently disclose any change in benefits, and any change in premium, resulting from the aging of the insured, policy duration, or any other factor, and provide that if the insurer retains any right to modify premiums in the future, that fact shall be disclosed.

Section 10127.8(c) provides that if the benefits of the advertised policy decrease with the insured's age or with policy duration while the premium remains approximately constant, that fact shall, in a print or broadcast advertisement, be disclosed in the same form and with prominence or visible duration equal to that given any positive description of benefits or the telephone number or address provided for further information or application, whichever is the most prominent.

Section 10127.8(d) requires a television or radio advertisement for term life insurance directed to individuals 55 years of age or older to contain in the spoken text the statement policy (or certificate) benefits and limitations should be carefully examined prior to purchase.

Section 10127.8(h) provides that the section applies to the advertisement of individual policies and any group policies or certificates delivered or issued for delivery in California, regardless of the situs of the contract.
notes: This is an advertising statute with a defined audience, individuals 55 or older as the commissioner assesses the whole advertisement. It governs what an advertisement must disclose, not what a policy must contain. Its list is still useful as a statement of which term features the Legislature treated as material: a stated termination age or period, premiums that change with age or duration, and benefits that shrink while the premium stays level.
